name: Theodore Roosevelt National Park
unique: Painted badlands where bison and wild horses graze among striped cliffs, the landscape that shaped Roosevelt's conservation ethic.
buzz: People call it a mini Badlands with more wildlife; the loop drive is excellent at dawn. Summer heat and ticks.

name: Theodore Roosevelt National Park North Unit
unique: The badlands unit of the park Roosevelt called his home, with bison and longhorn steers on the prairie dog towns and a scenic drive along the Little Missouri.
buzz: The bison and the cannonball concretions are the two things people photograph; the north unit is quieter than the south and the loop drive takes two hours.

name: North Dakota Heritage Center
company: State Historical Society of North Dakota
unique: The state museum with a full size Triceratops, a reconstructed homestead shack and galleries on the Mandan, Hidatsa and Arikara nations, free on the capitol grounds.
buzz: The adaptation gallery and the Native exhibits are the reasons to come and it is free; allow two hours and check the dome tour.

name: Maah Daah Hey Trail
unique: A 144 mile singletrack trail across the badlands connecting the two units of Theodore Roosevelt park, with water crossings and no shade.
buzz: Mountain bikers rate it among the best in the country and the trail is exposed and remote; carry more water than you think.

name: Fort Abraham Lincoln
customer: History families, cavalry buffs, school groups
unique: The reconstructed cavalry post where Custer's 7th Cavalry rode out for the Little Bighorn, with earthworks and a On-A-Slant Mandan village below the bluff.
buzz: The reconstructed barracks and the Mandan village are the two stops; the living history weekends bring the fort back.

name: Chateau de Mores
company: State Historical Society of North Dakota
unique: A 26 room hunting lodge built by a French aristocrat in the badlands, furnished as it was when he ran a cattle empire and a beef packing plant.
buzz: The house and the story of the Marquis are the visit and the view over Medora is the setting; it pairs with the national park.

name: International Peace Garden
unique: A garden that straddles the United States and Canadian border, with a floral clock, a peace chapel and 2,300 acres of prairie and forest.
buzz: The border crossing in the middle of the garden is the novelty and the floral displays are the summer draw; bring a passport.

name: Medora Musical
unique: A Broadway style revue about Roosevelt and the Badlands, staged in an outdoor amphitheater carved into a butte, with a live horse and a fireworks finale.
buzz: It is earnestly patriotic and surprisingly well produced; the setting is half the experience. Bring a jacket.

name: Plains Art Museum
unique: A regional art museum in a converted warehouse with a strong collection of Native and regional painting, free and open to the public.
buzz: The Native galleries and the studio space are the local favorites; it is small enough for an hour and the store is good.

name: Bonanzaville
unique: Forty historic buildings moved onto one site, from a prairie church to a barber shop and a steam train, telling the story of the Red River Valley.
buzz: The scale is surprising for a small city; the pioneer village is good for kids. Check the event calendar for threshing days.

name: Enchanted Highway
unique: Thirty two miles of giant scrap metal sculptures, a 60-foot tin family, pheasants, a grasshopper, built by a retired schoolteacher to keep his town alive.
buzz: It is a delightful detour with zero crowds; the sculptures are enormous and the story is better. Start in Regent.

name: Devils Lake
unique: A huge closed basin lake in the middle of the prairie that has risen for decades and swallowed farmland, with excellent fishing and pelican colonies.
buzz: Fishermen come for the walleye and the white pelicans are the surprise; the lake level has changed the shoreline and some roads end in water.

name: Fargo Theatre
unique: A 1926 atmospheric movie palace with a marquee on Broadway, restored and showing films, concerts and the Fargo Film Festival.
buzz: The organ and the ceiling are the reasons to look up and the festival in March is the local event; the seats are original.

name: Norsk Hostfest
unique: North America's largest Scandinavian festival, with Viking reenactors, lutefisk, wood carving and headline entertainment in a town of 48,000.
buzz: It is warm, weird and deeply sincere; the food is an adventure and the craft demos are excellent.

name: On-A-Slant Village
company: State Historical Society of North Dakota
unique: A reconstructed Mandan earth lodge village on the Missouri, with a interpreter in the lodge and a museum on the trade and the smallpox epidemic.
buzz: The earth lodge and the interpreter are the reason to come and the tour is short; it is included with Fort Lincoln.

name: Scandinavian Heritage Park
unique: A park with a full size replica stave church, a Danish windmill, a Finnish sauna and a Swedish Dala horse, celebrating the immigrants who settled the prairie.
buzz: The stave church is the photograph and the park is free; the Norsk Hostfest in the fall fills the city.

name: Cross Ranch State Park
unique: A park on a free flowing stretch of the Missouri with cottonwood forest, a canoe launch and trails through native prairie.
buzz: The river and the big cottonwoods are the reason to camp and the birding is good; it is quiet and the nearest town is small.

name: Dickinson Museum Center
customer: Families, fossil hunters, local history fans
unique: A museum with a badlands dinosaur hall, a pioneer wing and a collection of Depression glass, on the edge of the oil country.
buzz: The dinosaur exhibits are better than a town this size deserves and the staff are local; it takes 90 minutes.

name: Fort Buford State Historic Site
company: State Historical Society of North Dakota
unique: The frontier post where Sitting Bull surrendered in 1881, with the surviving commanding officer's quarters and the confluence of the Missouri and Yellowstone nearby.
buzz: The one standing building and the story are the visit; the site is remote and the confluence overlook is a short drive.

name: Grahams Island State Park
unique: A wooded island campground surrounded by Devils Lake, with a boat ramp, a swim beach and some of the best walleye water in the state.
buzz: The fishing is the draw and the campground is the base; the lake level rise has taken some of the shoreline.

name: Missouri-Yellowstone Confluence Center
company: State Historical Society of North Dakota
unique: An interpretive center where the two great rivers meet, the camp site Lewis and Clark described, with a trail to the confluence and a gallery on the fur trade.
buzz: The view of the two rivers running side by side is the reason to come; it is free and the birding on the flats is good.

name: North Dakota Museum of Art
unique: A university art museum in a former student union with a sculpture court, free and showing contemporary work that rarely reaches the state.
buzz: The sculpture court and the visiting shows are the reason to stop; it is free and the coffee bar is a local meeting spot.

name: North Dakota State Capitol
unique: A 19 story art deco skyscraper capitol on the prairie, the tallest building in the state, with an observation deck and a museum in the basement.
buzz: The observation deck and the art deco lobby are the reasons to go in; it is free and the grounds have a buffalo herd.

name: North Dakota State Fair
unique: The state fair in Minot with livestock barns, a midway, a rodeo and grandstand concerts, in the oil boom town of the north.
buzz: The barns and the horse pulls are the real fair and the concerts draw the region; parking is a walk and the heat is real.

name: Sheyenne River Valley Scenic Byway
unique: A 63 mile drive through the wooded Sheyenne valley with a 19th century mill, a scenic overlook and one of the few forested river corridors in the state.
buzz: The fall color is the season and the valley is a surprise after the flat prairie; the road is two lane and the towns are small.

name: Turtle River State Park
unique: A CCC built picnic shelter and a river winding through wooded coulees, with trails and a campground 20 minutes from Grand Forks.
buzz: The CCC shelter is the architecture and the trails are easy; it is a good half day and the fall color is the best in the region.

name: Chahinkapa Zoo
unique: A small zoo in a 76 acre park on the Red River, with bison, tigers and a carousel, run by a city of 8,000.
buzz: The park and the zoo together make a good afternoon with children; it is small and the carousel is the tradition.

name: Gingras Trading Post
company: State Historical Society of North Dakota
unique: The log trading post and house of a Métis fur trader, among the oldest buildings in the state, on the Pembina River.
buzz: The buildings are original and the story of the Métis cart trails is the history; the site is small and quiet.

name: Lewis and Clark State Park
unique: A park on the Missouri where the expedition camped, with a lake for walleye and a campground in the cottonwoods.
buzz: The fishing is the reason locals come and the lake is quiet; the park is small and the cottonwood shade is welcome in summer.

name: Turtle Mountain Scenic Byway
unique: A loop through the forested Turtle Mountains on the Canadian border, with lakes, a Chippewa casino and a landscape that rises out of the flat prairie.
buzz: The change from prairie to forest is the surprise and the fall color is good; the roads are quiet and the byway is unsigned in places.

name: Ukrainian Cultural Institute
unique: A cultural center with embroidered textiles, pysanky eggs and a Friday lunch of borscht and pyrohy, in a town settled by Ukrainian immigrants.
buzz: The Friday lunch is the local tradition and the collection is a surprise; call ahead, the kitchen runs on volunteers.
